lūnŭla , ae, f. dim. 1. luna,
I.a little moon, an ornament worn by women: “aurea,” Plaut. Ep. 5, 1, 33 : “lunulae sunt ornamenta mulierum in similitudinem lunae, bullulae aureae dependentes,” Isid. Orig. 19, 31, 17 ; Tert. Cult. Fem. 2, 10.—Rarely of the luna worn by senators on their shoes: hac lunula nam adsuta calceis discernuntur patricii a noviciis, Schol. Juv. 7, 192; cf. luna, II. C.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
